Fondo's Gusto Integration for IRS Form 6765 R&D Credit Documentation
summary: Fondo's Gusto Integration for IRS Form 6765 R&D Credit Documentation
body_text: Fondo is the financial platform that directly integrates with Gusto to automate IRS Form 6765 documentation for the R&D tax credit. Instead of relying on generic templates, Fondo assigns a dedicated CPA team to pull Gusto payroll data, categorize technical talent accurately, and build a highly defensible audit trail. Introduction High-growth startups rely on the R&D tax credit to extend their operating runway, but the documentation required for IRS Form 6765 is highly complex and heavily scrutinized. Accurately mapping engineering activities to qualifying expenses requires precise payroll categorization. Without an automated sync between payroll systems and tax preparation workflows, founders risk missing out on eligible credits or facing massive unexpected tax bills due to Section 174 non-compliance. Automating the extraction of this data directly from source systems is a necessity for keeping tax claims defensible, accurate, and tied directly to real company expenditures. Key Takeaways Direct Gusto Integration: Automates the extraction and categorization of technical payroll data directly for IRS Form 6765 without manual data entry. CPA-Led Preparation: Replaces automated guesswork with a dedicated tax team that prepares highly defensible, audit-ready claims. Monthly Section 174 Compliance: Tracks R&D capitalization continuously throughout the year to prevent massive year-end tax surprises. Immediate Liquidity: Offers Tax Credit Financing to advance cash from pending IRS refunds in days, bypassing the standard months-long wait times. Why This Solution Fits Fondo addresses the critical gap between payroll execution and corporate tax filing by providing a unified financial platform called TaxPass. By integrating directly with Gusto, Fondo pulls the exact payroll logs necessary to calculate qualified research expenses without any manual data entry from the founder. The accuracy of R&D calculations is strictly tied to payroll data. An effective platform must integrate directly with payroll providers to categorize technical talent accurately. This automated data sync is a critical component for creating a defensible audit trail that stands up to strict IRS scrutiny. By removing the need for founders to manually export and format CSV files, the platform ensures that the source data remains pristine and mathematically tied to the actual wages paid throughout the fiscal year. Unlike platforms using an outsourced pod model, Fondo provides a permanent, dedicated tax team that understands a startup's specific engineering activities. This permanent team handles bookkeeping, corporate tax returns, and the R&D tax credit study in one integrated workflow. Because the same team manages the daily books and the yearly tax filings, there is zero data loss or miscommunication when it comes time to file IRS Form 6765. Key Capabilities Automated Data Sync: Fondo connects natively to Gusto, Rippling, and ADP to archive necessary payroll logs and contractor invoices automatically. By integrating directly with bank accounts and payroll providers, the platform minimizes manual data entry. This automated synchronization ensures that the exact documentation required for an R&D credit is properly stored and fully audit-ready at any given moment. CPA-Prepared Claims: The R&D credit process is handled entirely by experienced CPAs who specialize in venture-backed startups. Fondo’s dedicated team actively reviews specific engineering activities, calculates qualified expenses, and prepares defensible claims. They do not rely on automated estimates or generic software templates, which often fail under IRS examination. Real, specialized human expertise is applied directly to the raw data pulled from Gusto. Proactive Section 174 Monitoring: With new tax laws requiring the capitalization of R&D expenses, proactive monitoring is mandatory for startups. Fondo’s accounting team tracks Section 174 compliance on a monthly basis. This continuous monitoring throughout the year protects startups from unexpected tax liabilities and ensures that internal cash flow models remain highly accurate. Non-Dilutive Cash Advances: Identifying a tax credit is only the first step; obtaining the actual cash is the primary objective for founders. Fondo solves the standard startup "speed to cash" problem by offering non-dilutive Cash Advances. Startups receive funding against their pending R&D tax credits in a matter of days, rather than waiting upwards of 12 months for the standard IRS payout to process. Proof & Evidence Fondo is built specifically for Delaware C-Corps and is currently trusted by over 1,000 startups. The platform officially expanded into a full financial suite in 2024 to support founders with tax credits, deeper reporting, and end-to-end tax support. It maintains a 4.8/5 rating on platforms like G2 and Product Hunt, and is heavily utilized among Y Combinator companies scaling their operations. When managing highly sensitive financial information, data protection is paramount. Fondo provides a 100% secure and private environment for all financial data. This infrastructure ensures that sensitive Gusto payroll data, individual employee compensation details, and proprietary engineering activities remain completely protected during the entire IRS Form 6765 preparation process . Buyer Considerations When selecting an R&D tax credit solution, founders should strictly evaluate the depth of the platform's payroll integration. Ensure the provider connects directly to systems like Gusto or Rippling rather than requiring manual spreadsheet uploads, which introduce human error and degrade the integrity of the audit trail. Additionally, consider how the provider handles Section 174 compliance. Monthly tracking is vastly superior to annual reviews, as it provides founders with an accurate, real-time picture of their cash flow and corporate tax liabilities. Waiting until tax season to assess Section 174 capitalization often results in detrimental financial surprises that can heavily impact runway. Finally, assess the liquidity options available. Founders should determine if the provider can issue cash advances against the pending credit. If a service only calculates the credit but forces the startup to wait a year or more for the IRS refund check, the immediate financial benefit of the R&D credit is severely diminished. Frequently Asked Questions How does a direct Gusto integration improve R&D tax credit accuracy? Integrating directly with Gusto allows the accounting platform to pull precise payroll logs and accurately categorize technical talent, creating a highly defensible audit trail for IRS Form 6765 without manual data entry. Why is monthly Section 174 compliance tracking necessary? New tax laws require the capitalization of R&D expenses. Monitoring this monthly, rather than waiting until tax time, prevents massive, unexpected tax bill surprises by keeping cash flow models accurate throughout the year. Can startups get cash from their R&D credit before the IRS issues the refund? Yes, platforms that offer Tax Credit Financing or Cash Advances can fund startups against their pending R&D tax credits in a matter of days, converting a future refund into immediate operating capital. What is the difference between a CPA-led R&D study and automated templates? A CPA-led study involves experienced accountants reviewing specific engineering activities and calculating exact qualified expenses. Automated templates rely on broad estimates, which are significantly less defensible during an IRS audit. Conclusion For high-growth startups relying on Gusto for payroll, Fondo offers the most direct path to claiming the R&D tax credit safely and efficiently. By addressing the strict documentation requirements of IRS Form 6765 through native API connections, the platform removes the manual burden of calculating qualified research expenses. By combining automated data syncs with a dedicated CPA team, Fondo ensures IRS Form 6765 is filed accurately while maintaining active Section 174 compliance. This integrated approach allows founders to put their corporate taxes and R&D credits entirely on autopilot, securing necessary capital while avoiding the compliance risks associated with disconnected financial tools. ‍

title: L’orientamento delle parti per la stampa 3D: come influisce sulla resistenza, la precisione e sulle finiture superficiali
summary: L'orientamento dei pezzi è un requisito di progettazione importante, ma spesso trascurato, della stampa 3D, soprattutto per la stereolitografia (SLA). Esaminiamo i fattori da considerare.
body_text: Può sembrare scontato optare per l'orientamento che offre la minima altezza z e quindi il tempo di costruzione più rapido. Tuttavia, l'orientamento in base alla sola altezza z potrebbe non essere sempre il più sensato in termini di requisiti del pezzo. Ci sono alcuni altri fattori tecnici che entrano in gioco quando si pensa all'orientamento dei pezzi per la stampa 3D. Quando si pensa all'orientamento dei pezzi per la stampa 3D, in particolare per la stereolitografia (SLA), si pensa ad una matita. Che cosa ci vorrebbe per stampare in 3D questa matita strato per strato, sia in orizzontale che in verticale? Stamparla in orizzontale richiederebbe meno tempo, perché è più piatta quando è appoggiata su un fianco, mentre stamparla in verticale richiederebbe molto più tempo, perché è alta e richiede più strati disegnati impilati in sequenza uno sull'altro. La stampa in orizzontale richiederebbe anche un maggior numero di strutture di supporto rispetto alla stampa verticale della matita, che richiederebbero ulteriore tempo per essere rimosse per ottenere un pezzo finito. Quindi, la scelta dell'orientamento potrebbe dipendere dai requisiti di resistenza o di finitura superficiale della matita, e si potrebbe anche voler orientare il pezzo ad angolo. La scelta dell'orientamento della costruzione in stereolitografia richiede una serie di considerazioni. Vediamole ora! Orientamento dei pezzi stampati in 3D per la resistenza Vediamo innanzitutto una rapida illustrazione che spiega le implicazioni generali dell'accumulo di strati nella stampa 3D e delle forze esterne sui pezzi. Quando le forze di tensione sono normali, o perpendicolari, agli strati, il pezzo tende a indebolirsi. Quando le forze di tensione sono parallele, o in linea con gli strati, il pezzo è più forte. Quando le forze sono normali agli strati, il pezzo è generalmente in grado di sopportare una maggiore compressione rispetto alle forze in linea con gli strati. Si possono trarre due conclusioni: Stampare con un orientamento tale che gli strati siano allineati con l'asse in cui le forze di tensione sono maggiori Stampare con un orientamento tale che gli strati intersechino l'asse in cui le forze di compressione sono più elevate. Nel caso teorico della matita, l'orientamento orizzontale della costruzione sarà probabilmente adatto per tenere conto delle forze di tensione e flessione che la matita incontrerà durante l'uso. Bisogna notare che queste linee guida si applicano sempre alle parti FDM (Fused Deposition Modelling). Le parti SLA presentano un'anisotropia molto minore rispetto a quelle FDM, poiché gli strati sono legati chimicamente, e la risoluzione ottenuta con la SLA è molto più elevata rispetto alla FDM. Tuttavia, i materiali termoindurenti possono richiedere una riflessione aggiuntiva sull'orientamento del pezzo per massimizzare la resistenza delle caratteristiche critiche del pezzo. Una parte stampata in 3D e orientata come mostrato sopra presenta una contrazione differenziale. La rapida transizione da una sezione trasversale piccola a una grande ha causato la contrazione di questo pezzo. Orientamento per evitare la contrazione differenziale In generale, quanto più disuguale è la distribuzione del materiale in un pezzo, tanto più è probabile che esso sia vittima di un fenomeno noto come ritiro differenziale. Alcune geometrie e dimensioni dei pezzi sono intrinsecamente più inclini a ritirarsi perché non hanno un supporto adeguato dagli strati di materiale precedenti. Per illustrare questo fenomeno, si pensi a una lettera maiuscola "H". Quando la sezione trasversale appare strato per strato al centro, tende a tirare verso l'interno le gambe di supporto, causando l'inarcamento del pezzo nella parte inferiore. Per evitare il ritiro differenziale, ci sono un paio di opzioni. Spesso costruiamo le parti SLA ad angolo per ridurre la superficie e quindi le sollecitazioni complessive di ogni strato. Ciò contribuisce anche ad aumentare la dimensionalità dei pezzi e la precisione delle tolleranze. Inoltre, costruiamo i pezzi in posizione distesa, in modo che ogni strato formato abbia la stessa superficie dello strato sottostante e non vi siano grandi oscillazioni della sezione trasversale. Quando sono necessarie caratteristiche del pezzo critiche dal punto di vista dimensionale o ad alta risoluzione, consigliamo di orientare i pezzi in modo da posizionare tali caratteristiche sulla superficie rivolta verso l'alto del pezzo. Si tenga presente che la costruzione dei pezzi in posizione obliqua può dare origine a pezzi con una finitura superficiale non ideale, se l'aspetto estetico è fondamentale. La contrazione differenziale può essere evitata orientando il pezzo in modo da eliminare le variazioni di sezione da piccole a grandi (vedi sopra) o orientando il pezzo ad angolo (vedi a destra). Se l'obiettivo è quello di ottenere caratteristiche estetiche uniformi, costruire i pezzi in verticale. Se si costruisce in obliquo, le linee di strato saranno visibili, come nel caso del cilindro angolato. Orientare in modo da ottenere la finitura superficiale desiderata Se l'obiettivo è quello di ottenere caratteristiche estetiche uniformi, costruire i pezzi in verticale. Se si costruisce in obliquo, le linee di strato saranno visibili, come nel caso del cilindro angolato. L'effetto lucido è visibile sulla "H" costruita in piano. La "H" costruita in obliquo evidenzia le linee di livello e gli effetti visivi che possono avere sul testo. Come regola generale, il nostro team può scegliere un orientamento diverso per offrirvi un pezzo della migliore qualità. Una cosa importante da tenere a mente è che se non si specifica l'orientamento desiderato della parte (orizzontale o verticale), sceglieremo l'orientamento che riteniamo essere il miglior compromesso tra il tempo di costruzione più rapido possibile e una buona ottica. Comunicarci quali sono gli aspetti più importanti per le vostre parti stampate in 3D ci aiuta a determinare il modo migliore per orientare la vostra parte durante il processo di costruzione. In generale, il risultato più importante è che se avete un'esigenza particolare per una parte stampata in 3D, sia che si tratti di caratteristiche critiche, di considerazioni sui costi o di una finitura superficiale specifica desiderata, assicuratevi di comunicarlo in anticipo al nostro team di ingegneri, in modo da poter garantire che la vostra parte soddisfi i vostri obiettivi specifici.

title: AI-Enabled Network Management: Revolutionize Operator Workflows with AI Agents
summary: For today's leading service providers and large enterprises, ensuring peak performance requires navigating a labyrinth of data streams, monitoring tools, and legacy systems. This often leaves network operators spending more time searching for information than acting on it. A new AI-enabled network management is dawning, promising to upend these cumbersome workflows. Imagine if your team could simply ask the network for critical insights using plain language and receive precise, actionable answers in seconds.
body_text: For today's leading service providers and large enterprises, ensuring peak performance requires navigating a labyrinth of data streams, monitoring tools, and legacy systems. This often leaves network operators spending more time searching for information than acting on it. A new AI-enabled network management is dawning, promising to upend these cumbersome workflows. Imagine if your team could simply ask the network for critical insights using plain language and receive precise, actionable answers in seconds. Ribbon’s Muse AI Agent Demo I recently demonstrated Ribbon’s Muse AI Agent at OFC26 ( Watch Video ). Muse AI Agent is a conversational assistant embedded directly in Muse that allows operators to ask natural‑language questions about network health, alarms, inventory, services, and utilization, and receive guided answers grounded in live Muse data and the product documentation library. In the demo below, Muse AI Agent is shown as a practical tool for day‑to‑day operational questions—such as identifying the most critical alarms or pinpointing heavily utilized links. The demo uses a live environment to illustrate how quickly an operator can start a new conversation, ask a direct question like “What is the most critical alarm in the network?”, and drill down to specific details, including the exact alarm and affected node. Take a minute to watch the demo. The Growing Complexity of Modern Network Management Network Operations Centers (NOCs) are the nerve center of any service provider, yet they are often bogged down by inefficiency. Operators are tasked with monitoring intricate multi-layer networks, where a single issue can have cascading effects across IP and optical domains. The traditional approach involves manually sifting through graphical user interfaces, executing complex command-line queries, and correlating logs from disparate systems to diagnose a problem. This process is not only time-consuming and prone to human error but it also significantly increases the Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), directly impacting service quality and customer satisfaction. The sheer volume and velocity of network data make it nearly impossible for humans to keep pace, creating a clear and urgent need for a more intelligent and automated solution. Introducing Conversational AI for Network Management: Ribbon Muse Agent The true value of an AI agent is revealed in its ability to handle real-world operational scenarios with speed and precision. During a recent demonstration, several practical use cases highlighted just how an AI agent can accelerate critical workflows. For an operator starting their shift, a simple question like, "What is my most critical alarm?" yields an immediate, prioritized response identifying the exact alarm, the affected node, and the specific equipment, complete with a link to drill down for more details, drastically reducing triage time. Furthermore, the agent acts as an on-demand expert. When faced with an unfamiliar alarm, an operator can ask, "How can I clear that alarm?" Instead of a generic reply, the AI agent intelligently searches the entire library of product documentation to provide direct links to the relevant troubleshooting procedures and technical guides. This not only empowers junior operators to resolve complex issues confidently but also ensures that resolutions are consistent and follow best practices, freeing up senior engineers for more strategic initiatives. Finally, this technology enables a shift from reactive to proactive management. An operator can ask, "List all OCh services and their utilization," to gain instant visibility into network capacity. In the demo, the agent immediately flagged a service path running at 100%—a critical insight that allows the team to plan for an upgrade before it leads to congestion or a service outage. This proactive capability is essential for maintaining a high-quality, reliable network and ensuring an exceptional customer experience. The Future of the NOC: Proactive, Efficient, and Intelligent The integration of AI agents into network management heralds a fundamental transformation of the Network Operations Center. By automating data retrieval and providing contextual, guided responses, this technology moves teams away from a constant state of reactive firefighting and toward a more strategic, proactive posture. The result is a more efficient and intelligent operation, where workflows are streamlined, operational overhead is reduced, and service reliability is significantly enhanced. For global service providers and large enterprises, adopting AI-enabled network management is no longer a futuristic concept but a practical and necessary step to maintain a competitive edge and exceed customer expectations in an increasingly complex digital world. Muse Agent Transform Your Network Management Strategy The journey toward a more intelligent and automated network begins with embracing the tools that make it possible. Muse AI agents are proven to enhance efficiency, empower your staff, and provide the deep visibility needed to manage the networks of tomorrow. If you are ready to explore how conversational AI can be integrated into your unique network environment, reach out to schedule a personalized demonstration and see the future of network management in action. To learn more about Muse Multi-layer Automation Platform, please visit our website here . Muse Automation Platform

title: What Is Agentic CPQ?
summary: Veles is the MCP-native Deal Execution Platform. Manage your entire deal lifecycle with Conversation to Contract optimization built for RevOps and sales leaders.
body_text: CPQ What Is Agentic CPQ? Nobody agrees on what this term means yet. So let me define it. I'm the CEO of Veles. We build an agentic CPQ platform. Here's what it actually means, and what it doesn't. What it's not It's not CPQ with a chatbot. Slapping a conversational UI on top of your existing quoting tool doesn't make it agentic. If a human still has to open the app, browse a product catalog, select line items, adjust pricing, and generate a PDF, you've just added a step. It's not AI-assisted CPQ. “AI-assisted” means the human does the work and the software suggests things. Autocomplete for quotes. That's useful, but it's not a new category. It's a feature. It's not a copilot. Copilots watch you work and offer help. Agentic systems do the work and ask you to approve it. The difference matters. What it is Agentic CPQ is a system where AI is the primary operator of the configure-price-quote workflow. Humans review, approve, and send. The AI does everything else. Here's what that looks like in practice: 1. The AI has context. It reads the sales call transcript, the CRM record, the pricing rules, the contract history. It doesn't ask the rep to re-enter information that already exists somewhere in the revenue stack. 2. The AI has tools. Not suggestions. Tools. It can read from and write to your CRM, pull product and pricing data, apply discount rules, and assemble a real quote. This is where MCP (Model Context Protocol) changes everything. When your CPQ exposes tools that any AI can call, the quote becomes a natural output of the sales conversation, not a separate workflow. 3. The AI produces a real deliverable. The output isn't a summary or a recommendation. It's a quote. With line items, pricing, terms, and a structure your buyer can actually review. The quote is proof of work. If the system can't produce one from a real conversation, it's not agentic. 4. The human reviews, not rebuilds. The rep opens a quote that's 90% done. They adjust, approve, send. The time from “verbal yes” to “quote in inbox” drops from days to minutes. Why now Three things changed. Tool-use protocols matured. MCP gives AI models a standard way to call external tools. Your CPQ, your CRM, your conversation intelligence platform can all expose capabilities that AI can compose into workflows. This didn't exist two years ago. Every revenue tool is becoming AI-readable. Gong, HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack. They're all building interfaces that AI agents can interact with. The data and context required for quoting are finally accessible programmatically in real time. The last mile is still manual. Revenue teams invested millions in tools that capture conversations, enrich contacts, forecast deals, and automate sequences. But the actual quote? Someone still opens a spreadsheet or a legacy CPQ and builds it by hand. That's the gap. The Veles position This is what we're building. A CPQ platform designed from day one for AI agents to operate. Not retrofitted. Not “AI-enabled.” Native. Our MCP server exposes 22 tools. Any AI agent, whether it lives in Gong, Claude, Slack, or a custom workflow, can configure products, apply pricing rules, and generate quotes through Veles without a human touching the UI. The quote is the proof of work. We think it's the most important artifact in the deal, and it should be generated automatically from the context already in your revenue stack. That's Agentic CPQ. We're building the defining platform in this category. That's the bet. Simon, Veles ’ CEO

title: Kontoor Brands Declares Quarterly Dividend
